prompt wording.name: System prompt v4: check the draft sentence by sentence, quote whole units, say only what the quotes say
prompt wording.mechanism: A new system prompt version (v4) that starts from v3 and changes only wording. The only code change is registering the version and adding a challenger config. v4 keeps every v3 rule and makes three changes. (1) It adds a step to "How to work": before calling submit_answer, the agent checks the draft one sentence at a time. Each sentence must have a quote that states it; if none does, the agent adds the page sentence or row that does, or deletes the sentence. Then the agent reads its quotes on their own and adds back any words a quote depends on: its subject, the rest of the sentence, a list item's lead-in, the row's other cells, the header. This is the "sentence-level coverage" idea from the iteration-2 changelog, done by the model before it submits rather than by a check that rejects submissions, so rejected_submissions cannot move. (2) It replaces v3's "(one sentence or less)" with "quote whole units". That length cap pushes the agent to cut quotes short. Many unquoted_on_page failures are exactly that: a row cut before its Adjustable cell, a key sentence cut mid-way, a fragment without its subject, a list item without its lead-in, the sentence after the quoted one. (3) It adds two rules for the kinds v3 never named: no additions of the agent's own (explanations, workarounds, comparisons, stronger wording than the quote), which covers beyond_quote and not_in_read_pages; and no sentences about the documentation itself, which covers about_the_docs. It also tightens the header-row rule (quote the whole row, first cell included, exactly as written), which covers headerless_row. Every change either makes the agent quote what it already relies on or makes it delete what it cannot quote, so support actually improves rather than the wording getting past the rubric.
prompt wording.change:
In C:/Users/USER/projects/agent-evals/agent-evals/src/agent_evals/agents/docs/prompts.py, add after SYSTEM_PROMPT_V3 (written with the same backslash line continuations as v3; the text below is the exact model-facing text):

# V4 (iteration 3): wording only, on top of V3. Error analysis of V3's 82 attempt-1 dev answers that fail
# fully supported: 157 unsupported claims, 82 of them on the page but unquoted (often cut-off quotes),
# 27 going beyond the quote, 27 about the docs, 16 headerless rows; 71 of the 82 answers had dispensable
# claims. Adds a sentence-by-sentence check before submit, whole-unit quotes, and rules for those kinds.
SYSTEM_PROMPT_V4 = """\
You answer questions about Amazon Web Services using ONLY the documentation snapshot you can reach through your tools. Do not answer from memory: AWS defaults and limits change, and your training data may be out of date.

How to work:
1. Use search_docs to find relevant pages. Try a different phrasing if results look off.
2. Use read_page to read the pages you will rely on. Never cite a page you have not read.
3. Before you submit, check your draft one sentence at a time. For each sentence that states a fact, find the quote that states it. If no quote states it, either add a quote of the page sentence or table row that does, or delete the sentence. Then read each quote on its own, as the reader will: if it only makes sense with words you left out (its subject, the rest of its sentence, the lead-in of its list, the other cells of its row, the column headers), quote those words too.
4. Finish by calling submit_answer. If it returns an error, fix what the error says and call it again.

Rules for submit_answer:
- Every sentence of your answer that states a fact must be backed by one of your citations: the page URL plus a quote copied word for word from that page. This applies to context, extra numbers, names of settings and recommendations just as much as to the main answer. Readers see only your quotes as evidence. If you cannot quote it, leave it out.
- Prefer a short answer in which every sentence is quoted over a longer one with unquoted context.
- Quote whole units: one complete sentence, one complete list item, or one complete table row. Never stop a quote before the part your answer relies on, and never drop the words that say what it is about.
- When you cite a table row, quote the whole row exactly as the page writes it, including its first cell, and also cite the table's header row as a separate quote, so the reader can tell which column each value belongs to. A row of values without its header proves nothing.
- Say only what your quotes say. Do not add your own explanations, reasons, workarounds or comparisons, and do not make a quote stronger than it is: keep the page's "may", "most" and "can", and do not add "only", "must" or "always". Do arithmetic or unit conversions only on numbers you have quoted, and check the result.
- Do not write sentences about the documentation itself (what it says, where it says it, or what it leaves out). State the quoted fact directly, or leave the sentence out.
- Missing context is never a reason to abstain: if the core answer can be quoted, give that and leave the rest out.
- If the question rests on a false premise, say so and correct it, with a citation.
- If the documentation you can reach does not answer the question, set abstained to true and explain what is missing. Abstaining is better than guessing.
- confidence is your probability (0 to 1) that the answer is correct.
"""

Then change the registry to: SYSTEM_PROMPTS = {"v2": SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2, "v3": SYSTEM_PROMPT_V3, "v4": SYSTEM_PROMPT_V4}. SYSTEM_PROMPT_V3 and every other text stay byte-identical, so v3's fingerprint and cache entries do not change. Nothing changes in agent.py: no new check, submission_problems is untouched, and require_number_coverage stays false. The prompt has no examples, so nothing is taken from dev or test cases.

Keep require_number_coverage off, as in default. The champion config stays configs/default.yaml with prompt_version: v3. Rolling back is a one-line change.
prompt wording.expected_flips:
Upper bound: all 82, since every kind is addressed. The "other" case, a wrong unit conversion, is covered by the rule to check conversions. The 4 not_in_read_pages answers are covered by the no-workarounds and no-own-reasoning rule.

Shape of the 82: 34 have one unsupported claim, 26 have two, 22 have three or more. 48 have a single kind: 31 unquoted_on_page only, 6 about_the_docs only, 6 headerless_row only, 4 beyond_quote only, 1 other. Fixing unquoted_on_page together with about_the_docs or beyond_quote would flip 45 each. 71 of the 82 have dispensable claims, and 72 are rated could_quote_instead yes or partly, so deleting or quoting is feasible almost everywhere. The 6 answers rated dispensable "no" need extra quoting, which the whole-unit rule targets (truncated rows, mid-sentence cuts).

Compliance discount: v3 already said "if you cannot quote it, leave it out", and 71 answers still carried dispensable claims, so restating a rule does little. The new parts are the explicit check step and the change in quote length. If each claim is fixed independently with p = 0.35 to 0.45: 34×p + 26×p² + 22×p³ ≈ 11.9+3.2+0.9 = 16 at p = 0.35, up to 15.3+5.3+2.0 = 22.6 at p = 0.45. Subtract roughly 2 to 4 of the 33 answers that are now fully supported and could break when longer quotes or new sentences are not verbatim. Net: about 12 to 19 of 115 answered attempts, i.e. +0.10 to +0.16. Further discount for Haiku's compliance. As a reference point, iteration 1's wording-only change flipped about 22% of the failing answers (+0.192 of 0.886). Applied to 82 failing answers that gives 18, but half that is more prudent for a second wording pass. Central estimate: about 10 net flips, judge_supported 0.308 to about 0.39 (+0.08; plausible range +0.05 to +0.14). That is well above the +0.03 detectability floor, which is about 3.5 answers.
prompt wording.risks: rejected_submissions: no new check, and submission_problems is unchanged, so only the markup and empty-citation rules can fire. Neither depends on quote length or answer length, so it should stay near 0.021. uncited_answer: the agent ends up citing more, not less, so no regression is expected. fabricated_citation: this is the real risk. Whole rows and whole sentences are longer strings to copy word for word; one dev answer already had a quoted row whose first cell differed from the page. Mitigations in the wording: "exactly as the page writes it" and "including its first cell". Also check that the verbatim matcher normalizes whitespace in markdown table rows. If fabricated_citation rises, the falsifier catches it. correct: deleting dispensable peripheral claims does not touch the core answer; only 16 of 157 unsupported claims are core, and the rule "missing context is never a reason to abstain" protects against dropping the answer. Correct could fall only if the agent deletes a core sentence it could have quoted; per-case-type and per-service checks catch that. wrong_abstention: stricter quoting can push a cautious model to abstain. That is why v4 states explicitly that missing context is not a reason to abstain and leaves the abstention rule unchanged (v3 had lowered wrong_abstention from 0.031 to 0.017). Watch this metric first. missed_abstention: the abstention criteria are unchanged; the no-additions rule makes confident made-up answers like the 'no plans to raise the limit' case less likely, so this should hold or improve. Case types and service areas: false-premise answers keep their own rule. Quota and lookup cases are the ones that depend on tables; they gain from the whole-row and header wording and are the most exposed to verbatim misses. Rubric-gaming check (constraint 2): every route to a flip either quotes the claim or deletes it. The one rewording route is turning "the docs say X" into "X", and it flips only when X itself is quoted. In the post-run recount of the challenger's failures, a reader should confirm that about_the_docs claims fell because they were deleted or turned into the quoted fact, not into hedges such as "I could not find...", which the prompt does not ask for. Cost and latency: slightly more output tokens for longer quotes, offset by shorter answers; possibly one more read_page per case.
prompt wording.falsifier: The change does not work if any of the following happens on dev (130 cases × 3 attempts, paired against v3). (a) The paired 95% CI on judge_supported includes zero, or the point gain is below +0.03. (b) Re-running the same per-kind error analysis on the challenger's attempt-1 failures shows unquoted_on_page still at 70 or more claims and beyond_quote at 24 or more, meaning the check step was ignored. (c) The gain comes with fabricated_citation, wrong_abstention or correct regressing with its interval, or with a case type or service area regressing on correct. (d) The reader check finds the about_the_docs drop came mostly from hedges rather than deletions or quoted facts. The answer look changes only slightly: no citation markers in the text, answers somewhat shorter, more and longer quotes. If the challenger's median answer length differs from v3's by more than 25%, constraint 5 applies: have a person spot-check 30 answers before trusting the judge's number.
prompt wording.why_this: Of the wording changes available, this one goes after the largest causes in the counts. unquoted_on_page is 82 of 157 claims and appears in 57 of 82 answers, 31 of them with no other kind. Many of those are cut-off quotes, a pattern v3's own "one sentence or less" limit encourages, and changing the quote-length rule is the most direct wording fix for it. The other new part is the check step. "Leave it out" was already in v3 and 71 failing answers still had dispensable claims. A procedure the agent runs on its draft just before submitting is more likely to be followed than a fourth restatement of the rule, and it is the iteration-2 changelog's "sentence-level coverage" idea without a rejecting check, so it avoids the rejected_submissions regression that sank iteration 2. Adding the beyond_quote and about_the_docs rules in the same version is necessary: they are the most common partners in the top pairs (45 flips each when fixed together with unquoted_on_page), so fixing unquoted_on_page alone would leave about 14 more answers failing. Other options are weaker. Numbered example answers risk looking like dev cases and lengthen the prompt. Asking for citation tags in the answer text changes how answers look to the judge (constraint 5). A rewording that only targets the rubric would break constraint 2. The champion v3 stays registered and byte-identical.

submit tool.name: Per-sentence citations in the submit_answer schema (submit_schema: per_sentence)
submit tool.mechanism: A change to the submit_answer tool's input schema and description. The answer is no longer one free-text string plus a separate list of citations. It is submitted as an ordered list of sentences, and each sentence carries its own citations, the quotes that back that sentence. The harness then turns this back into exactly what the graders and judge read today. answer is the sentence texts joined with single spaces, and citations is the deduplicated union of all per-sentence quotes in first-appearance order. The judge's input format does not change (plain prose answer, then a numbered quote list), and no citation markers appear in the text. No new submit-time rejection rule is added. The failure the error analysis found is mostly local: a quote of the neighbouring sentence, a quote truncated before the cell or clause that is used, a fragment that has lost its subject, or a table row without its header. The schema targets that by making the model write each quote right next to the sentence it is meant to prove, so a mismatch is visible at the moment of writing. The sentence that cannot get its own quote is then dropped, which is cheap because 71 of 82 such sentences are dispensable.

submit tool.expected_flips:
Ceiling, assuming every sentence is handled as instructed: the error analysis says 71 of 82 answers have dispensable unsupported content (5 partly) and could_quote_instead is yes for 47 and partly for 25. So nearly every failure can be fixed by quoting or dropping, which is exactly what the per-sentence slot asks for.

Mechanical estimate, with a per-kind fix rate under this schema: unquoted_on_page 0.55 (the failure is a neighbour, truncated or subjectless quote, which adjacency exposes), headerless_row 0.55 (the header must sit in the same sentence's citations), about_the_docs 0.45 (attribution rewritten as the fact, omission statements removed), beyond_quote 0.30 (has no quote, so it must be dropped), not_in_read_pages and other 0.2-0.3.

Sole-kind answers: 31 x 0.55 = 17.0, 6 x 0.55 = 3.3, 6 x 0.45 = 2.7, 4 x 0.30 = 1.2, 1 x 0.2 = 0.2, total 24.4.

Two-kind answers, derived from the pair counts: {unquoted, about} = 45 - 31 - 6 = 8, so 8 x 0.55 x 0.45 = 2.0. {headerless, unquoted} = 41 - 37 = 4, so 4 x 0.30 = 1.2. {unquoted, beyond} = 45 - 35 = 10, so 10 x 0.165 = 1.65. The remaining ~12 answers with three kinds or not_in_read_pages give about 1.0. Mechanical total about 30 of 82.

Compliance discount: v3's prompt already says "every sentence must be backed" and Haiku still left 82 of 115 answers short of that. Iteration 2's targeted mechanism moved only +0.020. So I halve the mechanical total for loose tagging (a nearby quote attached that does not state the sentence) and subtract about 2 answers that newly fail (a new non-verbatim or truncated quote, bullets merged into a sentence the judge reads differently). Central estimate: about 13 net flips of 115 answered attempt-1 answers, so judge_supported +0.11 (0.31 to about 0.42). Plausible range 6 to 20 flips (+0.05 to +0.17). The detectability bar of +0.03 is about 3.5 net answers, so even the low end should clear the gate.
submit tool.risks:
rejected_submissions (0.021): no new content rule is added. The only rejection paths are the existing uncited and markup checks (now run on the flattened answer) and schema-shape errors. With strict_tools true the API enforces the nested schema, so shape errors should stay near zero. Iteration 2 regressed this metric with a content check that fired on 38 of 390 attempts, and this change deliberately adds no such check. Residual risk: if strict mode is off or rejects the nested schema, local validation errors could rise, so check this on a 10-case smoke run first.

fabricated_citation (0.013): the main real risk. Each sentence carries its own quote, so answers will hold more distinct quotes, and each extra quote is another chance for Haiku to paraphrase instead of copy. The quote field text stays "Copied word for word from the page." and duplicates are merged, but watch it. If its interval excludes zero the gate fails, and the per-sentence data shows which sentences caused it.

uncited_answer: the same rule applies to the flattened list, and an answer with no quotes at all is rejected exactly as before, so it should not rise.

correct (0.959): the keyword grader reads the joined answer, and joining with spaces keeps phrases intact. Dropping extras could remove a must_include phrase that only appeared in a peripheral sentence, but the analysis says the core is quoted in all but 5 of 82 answers and only 6 answers have non-dispensable unsupported content. Low risk; read the per-category intervals.

wrong_abstention (0.017): the description says outright that removing an extra sentence never means abstaining. Low risk.

missed_abstention: making the model quote every sentence makes confident answers to unanswerable questions harder to write, so this metric would more likely improve than regress.

Per-category correct: no category-specific text, so no expected skew.

judge_supported validity (hard constraint 2): the gain comes from sentences being quoted by their own quote or removed, not from a change the judge can see. One gaming route exists: omission statements ("the docs do not say X") could be reworded as hedges ("I could not confirm X"), which the rubric exempts. The description tells the model to remove such sentences rather than reword them, and the 15-answer read in the gate procedure checks for it. Cost and latency: somewhat more output tokens (quotes repeated per sentence, about +10-20%), on a $0.0028 per-success base.
submit tool.falsifier:
Any of these would show the change does not work.
- On dev, the paired judge_supported difference has a 95% interval that includes zero, or a point estimate below +0.03.
- The stored sentences show loose tagging: in a sample of 30 accepted answers, many fact sentences have quotes that do not state them (for example under half share the sentence's subject and numbers). That would mean the slot is filled mechanically, and a re-run of the error analysis would find unquoted_on_page still in about 57 of the failing answers.
- fabricated_citation or rejected_submissions shows an interval excluding zero in the worse direction.
- The flips turn out to be omission or attribution sentences reworded into hedges rather than quoted or removed. Then the gain is rubric gaming, not better support, and the change must not ship even if the gate passes.
submit tool.why_this:
The dominant failure is unquoted_on_page: 82 of 157 claims, in 57 answers, and the only kind in 31. It is local: the agent quoted the sentence before or after, cut the quote before the cell or clause it used, or quoted a fragment that lost its subject. A flat citations list hides that, because the model checks coverage against a pool of quotes. Putting the quote in the same object as the sentence makes the model write the proving text next to the claim, so a mismatch is visible while writing, and a sentence that cannot get its own quote is simply left out. That is cheap, since 71 of 82 are dispensable. The same structure carries the header rule (13 headerless answers) and the attribution and omission rules (21 about_the_docs answers) to the sentence where they matter.

Alternatives within the mechanism are weaker:
- Index tags pointing into a flat citations list let the model tag a quote number without rereading the quote, which is exactly the loose behaviour that left v3 at 0.31.
- A required header field per citation reaches at most the 6 headerless-only answers, below the detectability bar.
- Rewording the flat description alone would mostly repeat v3's prompt.
- Any submit-time coverage rejection repeats iteration 2's rejected_submissions regression.

This change also adds no rejection path and keeps the judge's input in its current format. It also stores sentence-to-quote pairs, which the changelog's proposed structural check would need in a later iteration.

submit-time check.name: complete_table_citations: at submit time, widen each table-row quote to its whole row and add the table's header row
submit-time check.mechanism: A deterministic submit-time check, chosen by a config flag the way iteration 2 chose require_number_coverage, and run in the same _check_submission path. It differs from iteration 2 in what it does with a finding. The defect it detects (a quoted table row that is cut short, or that has no header) has exactly one correct fix, and that fix is text on the page the agent cited. So the harness applies the fix instead of sending the answer back. It never rejects anything. I measured why that matters on the champion dev run (docs-20261016-214710-02abb7). The detector fires on 111 of 349 answered attempts: 89 have a row with no header and 85 have a partial row. A rejecting version would bounce about 3x as many submissions as iteration 2's 38 did. More generally, no rejecting check can pass this gate. The call cache makes the challenger identical to the champion everywhere the check does not fire. Every flip of the target therefore needs at least one rejection. Reaching +0.03 means at least about 11 rejections spread over 4 or more cases, against zero offsetting differences elsewhere. That pushes rejected_submissions' paired interval above zero.

submit-time check.risks:
Target and correctness first:
- Constraint 2 (real support): the answers really are better backed. Each added quote is verbatim text from a page the agent itself cited: the header that gives a value its meaning, or the rest of the row the claim used. The reader now sees that evidence. Nothing is reworded and no claim is hidden. If a claim misreads a row, the full row makes the error visible to the judge and the reader. The honest limit: the agent's own quoting behaviour does not change, and the bulk of failures is untouched (unquoted prose in 57 answers, about-the-docs in 21, beyond-quote in 25).
- correct: cannot move. The answer text is byte-identical and the keyword grader reads only the answer. The same holds per case type and per service area, so gate condition 3 is safe by construction. Any change would be a bug.
- rejected_submissions: cannot move, because the change never rejects and the model sees the same "Answer received." All agent calls hit the cache, so the delta should be exactly 0.000.
- fabricated_citation: cannot rise. Every added or widened quote is checked with contains_quote before it is kept, and headers shorter than min_quote_chars (12) are never added. It can only fall, and only if a widened quote replaced an invalid one, which does not happen because the original matched the row.
- uncited_answer: unchanged; only answers that already have citations are touched.
- wrong_abstention and missed_abstention: unchanged, since abstained answers are skipped and abstained is never altered.
- unsupported_entity: can only fall, as more numbers now sit in quotes.
- judge_supported can fall only through judge randomness on the 20 already-supported attempts that get modified. Adding verbatim evidence cannot remove support.
- Wrong row: 4 of 236 row quotes were ambiguous and are left alone. A cell that also appears in prose is left alone unless the quote contains "|".
- Row length: the longest row is 1037 characters, so no cap is needed.
submit-time check.falsifier:
The proposal fails if any of these happen:
- On dev, the paired judge_supported delta against docs-20261016-214710-02abb7 is below +0.03, or its 95% interval includes zero.
- Of the 9 named cases (docs-ai-002, docs-ai-003, docs-ai-002-p3, docs-mix-086, docs-mix-056, docs-chg-016, docs-mix-057, docs-int-038, docs-int-042), fewer than 6 turn fully supported on attempt 1.
- Among the 111 modified attempts, the 1-to-0 flips come close to the 0-to-1 flips.
- The 30-answer human spot check of modified attempts finds that the judge credits header or row citations that do not actually back the claim.

Any nonzero change in correct, rejected_submissions, wrong_abstention or missed_abstention, or any rise in fabricated_citation, means the implementation leaks past the accepted path or adds an unverifiable quote. That is a bug, not a result.
submit-time check.why_this:
I simulated the alternatives within this mechanism on the champion's dev outputs.
- A rejecting table-header or full-row check fires on 111 of 349 answered attempts, against iteration 2's 38, which already failed the rejected_submissions condition.
- A narrower version, firing only when the answer uses words from unquoted cells or headers, still covers the roughly 16% of answers with a headerless or partial row (about 60 of 390).
- A sentence-level coverage check would fire on most of the 57 unquoted_on_page answers.
- More fundamentally, the call cache makes every non-fired attempt identical, so a rejecting check's rejected_submissions delta is at least its flip count. Any detectable gain (+0.03 is about 11 or more flips in 4 or more cases) comes with a regression whose interval excludes zero.
- Table rows are the one defect class where the fix is determined by the page the agent cited and needs no model judgement, so the check can repair instead of reject.

It is also the change with the cleanest audit: answer text unchanged, agent calls fully cached, only judge calls re-run on modified attempts (about $1).

A later iteration could extend the same in-place completion to prose quotes cut mid-sentence (docs-ai-005-p2, docs-core-002, docs-chg-022). I left that out to keep this to one change and because it would modify many more citations.

The judge's validation never included harness-completed citations. The answer text is unchanged, but 32% of answered attempts gain or widen a citation, so a person should spot-check 30 modified attempts before the judge's number is trusted.
